scams.name: Blue Hole Dive-Op Safety Cuts
scams.tldr: The shop is small, the cylinders are stacked neatly outside, and the photos on the wall show clear water at the famous Arch feature.
scams.description: The shop is small, the cylinders are stacked neatly outside, and the photos on the wall show clear water at the famous Arch feature. You sign a single-page waiver, get a five-minute briefing, and ride a pickup truck up the coast road to the dive site.
scams.avoidance: Verify the lead instructor's PADI or SSI number on the certification body's online check tool before paying. Inspect the regulator, BCD, and gauge on land before boarding any pickup truck to the dive site. Book Blue Hole and Canyon dives only through Reef 2000, Big Blue, or H2O — Dahab's three established operators with chamber-evacuation protocols. Refuse any Arch pass-through dive deeper than 56 meters unless your certification is Tec-Trimix. Never sign a single-page waiver — legitimate Dahab dive operators carry multi-page liability and insurance forms.
scams.location: Blue Hole, Bells, Canyon, dive-shop strip in Mashraba and Lighthouse

scams.name: Sharm Airport to Dahab Taxi Quote Switch
scams.tldr: The actual fair rate booked through any Dahab hotel runs 1,500 to 1,800 EGP (about $30 to $35), and "checkpoint fees" added en route push the curbside drop past $80.
scams.description: The actual fair rate booked through any Dahab hotel runs 1,500 to 1,800 EGP (about $30 to $35), and "checkpoint fees" added en route push the curbside drop past $80.
scams.avoidance: Pre-book your Dahab airport pickup through your hotel before you fly — every Dahab hotel arranges flat-rate transfers for 1,500–1,800 EGP. Walk past every freelance "taxi?" approach until you reach the official airport rank inside Terminal 1. Insist on Egyptian pounds and a written total — refuse all dollar quotes. Save your hotel's pickup-driver phone number before landing so you can confirm by call after passport control. If you must use the airport rank directly, agree on the full price in writing on your phone screen before luggage goes into the trunk.
scams.location: Sharm El Sheikh International Airport (SSH) arrivals taxi rank, Dahab bus station drop-off, hotel-arrival corridor

scams.name: Mashraba Bedouin Tea-Camp Bill Inflation
scams.tldr: And the bill at the end runs 800 to 1,200 EGP for hospitality framed as a cultural experience.
scams.description: And the bill at the end runs 800 to 1,200 EGP for hospitality framed as a cultural experience.
scams.avoidance: Refuse all unsolicited "free tea" sit-down invitations along the Mashraba and Lighthouse beach strips. Choose Bedouin cafés that display a printed menu with prices in Egyptian pounds visible at the entrance. Accept only what you ordered — politely send back any "free" plate that arrives unrequested. Confirm the total on your phone screen and have the server photograph it back before any second item is brought. Pay only at the end with exact small bills, never from a large note that invites "no change" haggling.
scams.location: Mashraba beach promenade tea camps, Assalah waterfront, Lighthouse beach Bedouin majlis tents

scams.name: Dahab Bungalow Hidden-Charge Trap
scams.tldr: Towels, AC, bottled water, and a service charge.
scams.description: Towels, AC, bottled water, and a service charge.
scams.avoidance: Insist on a printed itemized rate sheet at check-in — towel, AC, water, service, all listed in Egyptian pounds. Photograph the rate sheet on your phone before handing over any deposit. Book Dahab bungalows through Booking.com or Hostelworld where pricing is locked online and reviews flag surcharge patterns. Ask the owner directly: "Is anything in this room or service not included in the nightly rate?" Pay only the printed total on checkout — refuse any line item that did not appear at check-in.
scams.location: Mashraba budget bungalow strip, Lighthouse beach camps, Assalah backpacker dorms

scams.name: Camel Ride on the Promenade Ransom
scams.tldr: Claiming the animal will not kneel until you pay.
scams.description: Claiming the animal will not kneel until you pay.
scams.avoidance: Refuse to put any rider on a camel until the full price and route are typed on your phone and the handler photographs it back. Walk past camel approaches on the Mashraba promenade unless you are actively planning a ride. Pay only at the end after the rider is back on the sand, from a small-denomination stack. Use the Tourist Police number 126 if a handler refuses to dismount your child after a verbal price was agreed. Book camel experiences only through your hotel concierge, which contracts with vetted handlers at fixed rates.
scams.location: Mashraba beach promenade, Assalah waterfront, Lighthouse beach approach road

scams.name: Assalah Souk Currency Short-Count
scams.tldr: The receipt shows the agreed total because the count was wrong, not the math.
scams.description: The receipt shows the agreed total because the count was wrong, not the math.
scams.avoidance: Exchange currency only at a CIB, QNB, or Banque Misr ATM in Dahab town — never at a street counter or hotel desk. If you must use a counter, count the stack twice in front of the changer before stepping back from the window. Familiarize yourself with EGP note colors before you arrive — 50 piastre is brown, 10 EGP is bright red, 50 EGP is purple, 100 is olive. Refuse any change that includes coins or notes from other currencies mixed in. Bring the smallest denomination of dollars or euros you can — small bills exchange at a slightly lower rate but eliminate the multi-hundred short-count exposure.
scams.location: Assalah Square money changers, Mashraba souvenir shops with money-changing side hustles, hotel-lobby cash desks
